headline: Models infer cell states and interactions from spatial transcriptomic and histology data
label: Spatial Single Cell Omics Methods
summary: Spatial single-cell methods now predict expression from histology and integrate multi-omics, but cross-patient transfer remains limited.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of cell-level organization from spatial, multi-omic, or imaging data, with methods judged by what they can separate and transfer. SVC models subcellular transcript localization with a Vision Transformer, and Alpha Spatial predicts cell-level gene expression from histology under language conditioning across tissues and gene panels. SMODER uses RNA as an anchor for asymmetric spatial multi-omics deconvolution, while Cis-TERN integrates scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq through a directed bipartite graph and network diffusion to infer pseudotime. CellNet pretrains on 231 million single-cell profiles across 40 species, integrating DNA-derived gene identities with RNA expression. Newer contributions emphasize large-scale cross-modal pretraining and histology-conditioned prediction, yet the CosMx glioma point-process study reports limited cross-patient transfer, so generalization remains the open constraint.
